title: Config errors with their own classes
hints: Give `MissingKeyError` an `__init__(self, key: str)` that calls `super().__init__(f"missing key: {key}")` and stores `self.key = key`.

In `read_port`, turn low-level errors into your own: catch `KeyError` from `config["port"]` and `ValueError` from `int(...)`, and re-raise with `raise ... from None`. Check the range after the conversion succeeds.
In `collect_ports`: `try: port = read_port(cfg)`, `except ConfigError as err: errors.append(str(err))`, `else: ports.append(port)`. Catching the base class also catches `MissingKeyError`.
